result.summary: Manual review of the assigned obligations, lld:invariant:2 and lld:invariant:5. It uses only the supplied diffs and is not a canonical CR. I found no concrete, reachable defect in the supplied files. The IPC transport sources (shared TypeScript IPC, Kotlin UnixSocketDaemonRpc and DaemonGatewayService) and the daemon gate source (management-enablement.ts) were not supplied. Invariant 2 therefore cannot be verified directly. Invariant 5 holds on the test evidence, under the user's authorized correction that runtime management is enabled by default while releaseEnabled stays false.

obligations.evidence: The supplied tests point toward compatibility but cannot show it. connection-manager-compatibility.test.ts runs the legacy-facing JUnit classes Sc2DaemonGatewayTest (3 tests) and UnixSocketDaemonRpcParseTest (13 tests) plus the TypeScript compatibility cases. connection-project-server.ts uses the existing IpcServer and directDispatch, with no new storage path. The sources for the one-shot IPC API and the Kotlin transport were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the public signatures are unchanged or that the persistent lane sits on the same boundary. The JUnit tests were not run, and I did not read their pass results.

connection-manager-release.test.ts (CM-S5-GATE) asserts inventory and acceptance matrix releaseEnabled=false. It also asserts runtimeEnabled=true, matching the authorized correction. External prerequisites other than the two live-UI items must match /^pending/. VSCodeLiveUI is 'completed-user-reported' (0.5.23) and JetBrainsLiveUI is 'deferred-user'. A forged gates.json claiming ready=true with all scopes is rejected by verifyConnectionManagementRelease, so consumer coverage cannot stand in for the producer proofs. The parity test asserts corpus.releaseEnabled=false and corpus.fixturesAreAcceptance=false. Limitation: management-enablement.ts was not supplied, so the gate logic itself was not inspected. The test-run results were not seen.

limitations: test-fixtures/connection-management/v1/manual-orders.parquet is binary and only its size and hash were supplied, so its content was not assessed. The corpus.json that the manifest hash refers to was not supplied.
The IPC transport sources, daemon management-enablement.ts, the Kotlin and TypeScript production code behind the tests, and the S005 JSON and HTML artifacts were not supplied.
No test results were supplied, so none of the tests were verified as passing.
VS Code 0.5.23 manual testing is user-reported and JetBrains live UI is deferred; I did not treat either as passed.
SQL Server, provider-service and positive worker-affinity coverage remain pending.
The full-sweep failures and timeouts were not treated as evidence of a defect.
This review is not a canonical CR and does not approve BUILD.
evidenceRequests: Diff or source of the shared TypeScript IPC client (one-shot API plus persistent lane) and the Kotlin UnixSocketDaemonRpc and DaemonGatewayService, to verify that one-shot signatures are unchanged for lld:invariant:2.
src/daemon/db/management-enablement.ts, to confirm the default runtime policy and that verifyConnectionManagementRelease keeps releaseEnabled false for lld:invariant:5.
JUnit XML or tap output for the Sc2DaemonGatewayTest and UnixSocketDaemonRpcParseTest runs.
